To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reductions in atmospheric emissions of Cd have not necessarily led to reductions in Cd in aquatic food webs because the reductions in acidity in some lakes have led to increased Cd in organisms.
reductions in the atmospheric deposition of cadmium have led to reductions of cadmium in the water of some lakes but have led to increases in the cadmium in some lake food webs.

reductions in atmospheric emissions of cadmium have led to decreases in cadmium levels in lake water, but that increases in cadmium have been observed in some aquatic animals, and that this apparent contradiction is explained by the simultaneous reduction in lake water acidity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of atmospheric emissions of toxic metals on aquatic food webs.
the effects of atmospheric emissions of toxic metals from smelters on lakes.

the effects of acid deposition on the aquatic ecosystem, with particular reference to the effects of metals and the role of the aquatic food web in the transfer of metals from the water column to the sediments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk to aquatic organisms from cadmium has increased in some of the lakes we have studied.
the effects of reductions in atmospheric Cd deposition have not been as simple or as straightforward as expected.

reductions in emissions of atmospheric Cd have resulted in a reduction of the amount of Cd in the lakes but have also resulted in increased concentrations of Cd in some aquatic organisms, especially fish, and that the increased concentrations of Cd may have adverse biological effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reductions in atmospheric emissions of Cd have led to increases in Cd in some aquatic animals.
the effects of atmospheric pollution can be long lasting and that the recovery of lakes may be more complex than previously believed.

the reduction of emissions of Cd and other metals from smelters has led to improvements in lake chemistry, but that the benefits of this change have been offset by increases in metal concentrations in animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reductions in atmospheric emissions can be beneficial, but the beneficial effects may not occur for some time and the effects may be different than expected.
the toxicological risk from metals can increase even as emissions decline.
the effects of acidification and metal emissions are interrelated and cannot be considered independently.
